findings.passage: “This issue should not be controversial,” Hoadley said. “The people I represent want secure elections. In Michigan, I recently voted to stop the foreign funding of ballot initiatives in our state. We should all be in favor of protecting the integrity of our elections here in the United States. It really is a matter of common sense. Only verified U.S. citizens should be allowed to cast a ballot.”
findings.note: House caucus release in his name. The release says he supports the federal SAVE Act (proof of citizenship to register, photo ID to vote in federal elections) and that the Michigan House adopted a resolution urging Congress to pass it. He says only verified citizens should vote.

findings.passage: “We need to make it easier for our election officials to administer our elections according to the law,” said Hoadley (R-Au Gres). “With easily accessible proof of citizenship, we can better protect the integrity of the ballot.”
findings.note: House caucus release announcing he backs a bill that would put an eagle emblem on state-issued ID given to U.S. citizens, so election officials can see citizenship status when checking ID.
subjects: proof of citizenship on state ID

findings.passage: “Every eligible voter in Michigan needs to have confidence that our elections are being held securely,” Hoadley said. “A straightforward, recognizable designation of U.S. citizenship on state-issued identification is a very reasonable and straightforward step toward making those distinctions clearer.”
findings.note: Same release. He calls the citizenship marking on state ID a reasonable step.
subjects: proof of citizenship on state ID

findings.passage: “The inaccuracy of Michigan’s voter rolls is a legitimate concern,” Hoadley said. “Inaccurate information in the QVF can undermine voter confidence in the system. After failed lawsuits to clean up to rolls, my bill simply instructs the Secretary of State to send postage to a voter to verify the most accurate voter information is on file.”
findings.note: House caucus release on his House Bill 4356, which would have the state mail return cards to voters who have not voted in 10 years and remove those who do not respond. The release says the bill was referred to the Election Integrity Committee.

findings.passage: “Voters must have confidence that every ballot has been counted before their officials assume office. We need these kinds of measures in place to ensure that we can have firm public trust in these outcomes.”
